chunks: He said: Abu Ubaidullah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me, he said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Abdul Rahim al-Sajistani narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Asim, from Muhammad ibn Bishr, who said:
When Ibn al-Zubair expelled Ibn Abbas, may Allah have mercy on him, to al-Taif, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote to him:

As for what follows, I have been informed that Ibn al-Kahiliyyah has driven you out to al-Taif. May Allah, exalted be His name, raise your mention through that, grant you great reward, and lift from you a burden.
O cousin, indeed only the righteous are tried, and indeed honour is bestowed only upon the virtuous. And if you were rewarded only in what you love, then your reward would be little.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you.'
And this is something I have no doubt is good for you in the sight of your Creator. May Allah grant you great patience in adversity and gratitude in bounties. Surely He has power over all things.

When the letter reached Ibn Abbas, he replied: As for what follows, your letter has reached me, in which you console me regarding my exile, and you ask your Lord, exalted be His name, to raise my mention through it. And He, the Most High, is capable of multiplying the reward, and benefiting by His favour, and granting more of goodness. I do not wish that what Ibn al-Zubair perpetrated against me had been perpetrated by the enemies of God's creation, seeking thereby to increase my good deeds, and for what I hope to attain through it of the pleasure of my Lord.

O my brother! Indeed the world has turned its back and indeed the hereafter has drawn near. So perform good deeds. May Allah make us and you among those who fear Him in the unseen and act for His pleasure in private and in public. Surely He has power over all things.

key_terms.البلوى: Adversity, trial - a divine test of the believer's faith and patience
key_terms.الكاهلية: al-Kahiliyyah - a derogatory reference to Ibn al-Zubair, alluding to his maternal lineage from the Banu Kahil tribe
key_terms.رضوان: Divine pleasure/approval - the ultimate goal of the believer's patience in trials

ai.seo_question: What letter did Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah write to Ibn Abbas when he was exiled to al-Taif?
ai.summary: This hadith records an exchange of letters during the political turmoil of the second fitna (civil war) in early Islamic history. When Abdullah ibn al-Zubair expelled Abdullah ibn Abbas to al-Taif around 64-73 AH, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah (son of Imam Ali) wrote to console him, reminding him that trials befall the righteous, quoting Quran 2:216. Ibn Abbas replied with remarkable faith, saying he would not even prefer that the enemies of God had done this to him rather than Ibn al-Zubair, since he hopes for divine reward through this trial.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 3. He said: Abu Ubaidullah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me form Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Abdul Rahim al-Sajistani, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Asim, from Muhammad ibn Bishr, who said:
When Ibn al-Zubair expelled Ibn Abbas - may Allah bless him with mercy, to al-Taif, Muhammad ibnal-Hanafiyyah, may Allah bless him with mercy, wrote to him:
"I am informed that Ibn al-Kahiliyya has driven you out to al-Taif. That way Allah, Most High may exalt your name, and grant you great reward, and lift from you the burden.

O brother, (in this world) the trials are for the righteous, and blessings of honour are conferred upon the virtuous. If your reward were to be only in the things you like, then your rewards would be be too few.
For Allah says (in the Qur’an): ’... and you may dislike a thing which is good for you.’ [2:216].

And I have no doubt that the situation you are in is good for you in the sight of Allah. May Allah grant you great patience in this adversity, and enable you to be grateful for (His) bounties. Surely, He has power over all other things."

When the letter reached Ibn Abbas, he replied: "Your letter has reached me, in which you consoled me on whatever has happened to me, seeking your Lord to exalt my name. Surely, He has power to augment the reward, and to benefit by His favours and to grant more of goodness. I do not like the treatment meted to me by Ibn al-Zubair any more than had it been perpetrated by the enemies of mankind, and thus increase my reward. Nor did I expect to earn my Lord’s pleausre through his efforts.

O my brother! The world has indeed turned its back and the hereinafter has shadowed. So perform good deeds. May Allah count you and me among those who fear Him, the Unseen, and who act to earn His pleausre, publicly or in privacy. Surely, He has power over all."
